thread:
mira: Hey folks — saw a perf regression on continuous decode when requests include tool calls + structured outputs. Throughput drops ~18% and p99 latency spikes. Anyone else?

alex: Yep, noticed it on canary yesterday. Repro: mixed chat workload where ~12% of responses trigger a tool call (function webhook).

chen: Quick summary of what I think is happening: when model emits the stop-token sequence for a tool call we mark request as 'paused' and move it out of the active decode batch. That forces the batch to shrink early and flushes KV cache decisions; other requests in the batch lose batching density.

ben: Data: ran 10k requests on ded-sim with continuous batching enabled. baseline (no tools): 1200 reqs/s. with tool calls: 980 reqs/s. p99 from 210ms -> 340ms. raw profiler snippet:```
kernel: aten_gpt_fused  steps/s=105.6
kernel: quant_attn_v2   steps/s=98.3
batch formation avg size: 6.2 -> 4.8
kv-attach ops increased +14% (alloc/copy)
```

mira: Also seeing token budget used poorly — paused requests still hold onto their token budget reservation which prevents grouping short requests into a compact batch.

alex: Two root causes we flagged: (1) queue policy doesn't prefer short-latency requests once paused ones remain reserved, (2) kernel selection & packing assumptions expect steady decode per request; pauses break that distribution.

chen: Small experiment: change queue_policy from FIFO->prefer-short, and set token_budget_target=32 for interactive tier. Result: batch size recovered to ~5.8 and throughput to 1120 reqs/s, p99 down to 260ms. Not perfect but much better.

ben: Notes on KV behavior: when we pause we currently keep KV cache pinned on the serving GPU and set request state to PAUSED. That keeps memory stable but increases footprint. Reattaching later needs a KV replay or in-place resume. The in-place resume avoids recomputing KV but forces kernel path to handle discontinuous lengths which hurts fused kernel throughput.

mira: Options discussed in meeting: 1) Move paused requests onto a 'paused' queue and release their token budget immediately (let others use the tokens). On resume, re-acquire budget and try to re-batch. 2) Implement a small 'resume window' where resumed requests are immediately eligible for re-batching within X ms. 3) Special-case kernels: fast-path kernels that tolerate KV reattach cost better (e.g., non-fused fallback).

alex: Implementation tradeoffs: releasing budget helps batch formation but increases burst pressure and possibly SLO violations if resumed reqs can't get budget back quickly. Also more complicated accounting for quota/cost metrics.

chen: Kernel selection idea: use light-weight estimator that picks 'resume-safe' kernel if paused fraction > T. i.e., if >10% of active set are paused/resumed in last 60s, switch to kernel with better single-step latency even if lower throughput to avoid p99 spikes.

ben: Profiling raw numbers for kernel swap penalty: when switching from fused->resume-safe: cold swap cost ~9ms for kernel load + ~2% throughput loss steady-state for long sequences but p99 improves because stalls are shorter.

mira: We should also consider signal at inference level: can model emit an explicit special token to indicate imminent tool call vs normal stop? Right now stop tokens are ambiguous. If model emits `__TOOL_HANDOFF__` we could treat it like a soft pause and continue decoding other requests without freeing token budget. That requires model/eval changes though. :thinking:

alex: Another practical mitigation: extend batching horizon by a few tokens (token_lookahead=2). If a request emits stop but we suspect a tool call, wait up to N tokens to see if others arrive and/or resume quickly, then re-batch. Reduces immediate flushes but increases latency for true-fast completions.

chen: Repro script I used:```bash
# spawn mixed workload: 88% chat, 12% toolcall
ab -n 10000 -c 64 \"http://canary.internal/redwood/generate?mix=tool12&continuous=1\"
# profiler collect: rt-prof --pid $(pgrep runtime) --out /tmp/pprof.pb
```

ben: We need an A/B: (A) release prefer-short + token_budget_target=32 + resume-window=50ms, (B) token_lookahead=2 + keep-budget-on-pause. Measure cost delta and p99.

mira: Quick ask: can infra flip prefer-short on canary for 2 hours? I can run the A/B and collect traces.

oncall-bot: change-request registered: toggle queue_policy=prefer-short on canary-cluster for 2h. ticket=#INF-4382

alex: Great. I'll also add a kernel-chooser flag (resume_threshold=0.1) behind runtime.experimental so we can measure without rolling prod.

chen: One last gotcha — structured outputs with nested tool calls (tool calls emitting more tool tokens) create multi-pause chains that amplify the issue. Our plan should account for recursion depth and maybe cap re-batching attempts to avoid pathological churn.

mira: Awesome. I'll run the A/B when canary flips and post perf dumps here. If we get the 85-90% recovery we can roll to staging. Thanks team :raised_hands:
